summary: The narrator receives a text message from Checker, who has just returned to LA, inviting them to get together. The invitation feels surreal to the narrator, who sees themselves as someone unused to social life and more accustomed to work and threats. Reflecting on a visit from Arthur, the narrator begins to wonder whether people are not all bad and whether it might be fine not to drink alone that night. The narrator replies accepting, with a joking condition about a new Colt 1911 and signs off as Cas.
one_line: Cas, a lonely and guarded narrator, reluctantly accepts a drinking invitation from Checker after a text arrives in LA.
key_facts: The narrator receives a text message from Checker, who has newly arrived back in LA.
The narrator describes a strange, fizzy feeling in their chest when the message arrives.
The narrator sees the invitation as surreal, like watching someone else's life.
The narrator contrasts their usual texts, which are about work or death threats, with the friendly invitation.
The narrator thinks about Arthur's visit before deciding how to respond.
The narrator reflects that maybe people weren't all bad, at least not all the time.
The narrator considers that it might not be so awful not to drink alone tonight.
The narrator replies that the invitation works as long as their new Colt 1911 counts.
The narrator's reply ends with 'See you at 8.' and is signed Cas.
